why: Eager content is what every visitor downloads and decompresses before the first prompt. It grew silently once: an eager xkeyboard-config tree (293 files, 3,332,352 bytes) took the compressed shell from 1,047,839 to 1,436,395 bytes. The composer fails the build when the image exceeds these limits, so growth is always a reviewed change to this file. The November 2026 measurement also accounts for the existing image-owned game/ROM dispatchers, page terminal and preview publishers, Rust login profile, and web-stack/WordPress-family session-client descriptors. These bootstrap files route launches and exchange input before the optional runtime archives are selected or fetched; they remain in the base image. The develop integration also registers 21 additional lazy manual archives: their path catalogs must be available for lookup before archive contents are fetched. After placing npm manual aliases alongside npm, the normal image uses 2,384,338 eager bytes in 146 files and 1,107,317 compressed bytes. Bash (2,064,173 bytes) and login (98,565 bytes) remain necessary before the first prompt. Keep the eager-byte and file ceilings unchanged; a 1,110,000-byte compressed ceiling leaves 2,683 bytes of headroom for this measured composition. The GNU build tools (images/vfs/lib/init/dev-tools.ts) add nine lazy archives and 32 lazy programs; their path catalogs, about 1,500 entries (594 from autoconf-archive's macros, 518 from Texinfo's Perl modules), add 7,294 compressed bytes and no eager file bytes. Catalogs must be present at boot for the paths to resolve before an archive is fetched. A 1,117,000-byte compressed ceiling leaves 2,389 bytes of headroom. CMake adds three lazy programs and cmake-data.zip, whose path catalog has 4,355 entries (2,506 in share/cmake-4.5/Help, the reStructuredText `cmake --help-*` reads, and 1,760 in Modules), and cmake-docs adds 26 pages. Two partial shells, both with cmake-docs, that differ only by the cmake package measured 739,938 and 830,011 compressed bytes, so CMake adds 90,073 compressed bytes and no eager file bytes. The canonical shell with the GNU build tools, their pages, Meson, Ninja and CMake measures 1,205,642 compressed bytes; a 1,208,000-byte compressed ceiling leaves 2,358 bytes of headroom. On LLVM 23 with the SDK sysroot staged from declared inputs, the canonical shell measures 2,386,249 eager bytes in 145 files and 1,197,991 compressed bytes, within the unchanged limits. The Go toolchain's 2,793 indexed archive entries must be available for path lookup before the first fetch. The 35,639,840-byte archive remains deferred. With its catalog the canonical shell measures 2,386,251 eager bytes in 145 files and 1,274,473 compressed bytes, an increase of 76,482 compressed bytes over the recorded baseline.
measurement: maxEagerBytes and maxEagerFiles cover regular files whose bytes are stored in the image (not deferred to a lazy file or lazy archive), counted once per inode. maxCompressedBytes is the size of the zstd-19 shell.vfs.zst. images/vfs/scripts/image-eager-budget.ts measures them in the composer; `xtask vfs-image describe` on the built image agrees (entries with kind file and a content_sha256). measured records the image when these limits were last set; each limit may sit at most 5% above it, except that the file count may always have 4 files of slack.
raising: First ask whether the new content can be lazy: programs belong in SHELL_LAZY_BINARY_SPECS and optional data in SHELL_LAZY_DATA_ARCHIVE_SPECS (images/vfs/scripts/shell-lazy-archives.ts). If it must be present at boot, raise the limits in a commit whose message names the content, its size, and why it must be eager, and update measured to the new image. When content shrinks, lower the limits in the same change. See docs/package-management.md, Image eager-content budgets.
